title: Honor the lines argument in MCPManager.Logs
body:
## Summary
`MCPManager.Logs` and `ProcessManager.GetProcessLogs` both take `follow` and `lines` and ignore both: they return the whole log file. The same body is copied in two places.

## Evidence
Checked at `6ab6811`, under `control-plane/internal/mcp/`.

- `manager.go:328` `func (m *MCPManager) Logs(alias string, follow bool, lines int)`; the body at `:336` says `// TODO: Implement follow and lines functionality` and returns `os.Open(logFile)`.
- `process.go:401` `func (pm *ProcessManager) GetProcessLogs(alias string, follow bool, lines int)` has the same body and the same TODO (line 409).
- `ls internal/mcp/*_test.go` finds no test file, so neither is covered.

## What to do
Put the log-file lookup and the `lines` handling in one helper that both methods call. When `lines > 0`, return only the last `lines` lines of the file; when `lines <= 0`, return the whole file as today. Leave `follow` out of scope: say in the doc comment that it is not supported yet and narrow the TODO to `follow`. Keep the `io.ReadCloser` return type. Add `manager_test.go` that builds a manager over `t.TempDir()` with a log at `packages/mcp/<alias>/<alias>.log`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] For a 10-line log, `lines=3` returns exactly the last 3 lines; `lines=0` and `lines=-1` return all 10; `lines=50` returns all 10.
- [ ] A missing log still returns the `log file not found for server <alias>` error.
- [ ] The two methods share one implementation (no duplicated body).
- [ ] `go test ./internal/mcp/...` passes offline, and `go vet ./internal/mcp/...` is clean.

title: Make the agent counts in README.md match the files
body:
## Summary
`README.md` gives two different counts for the same thing (88 and 83 specialized agents), and none matches the files. Its structure tree also shows folders at the repo root that live under `.hanzo/agents/`.

## Evidence
Checked at `6ab6811`.

- "88 specialized agents": `README.md:22`, `:37`, `:60`, `:763`, `:772`. "83 specialized AI agents": `:49` and the tree comment at `:269`.
- `ls .hanzo/agents/definitions | grep -v '^README' | wc -l` prints `108`. The role-based table at `README.md:326-366` lists 16 of them, which leaves 92, not 88 or 83.
- "42 development tools": `README.md:49`, `:62`, `:278`, `:765`. `ls .hanzo/agents/tools | wc -l` prints `43`.
- "15 workflows" is right: `ls .hanzo/agents/workflows | wc -l` prints `15`.
- The tree at `README.md:266-281` draws `agents/`, `workflows/` and `tools/` at the root; `ls agents workflows tools` finds none of them.

## What to do
Pick one counting rule and write it down in the README (for example: specialized = files in `.hanzo/agents/definitions/` that are not in the role-based table). Recount, then make every count in the file agree with it and with `ls`. Redraw the tree with the real `.hanzo/agents/` layout.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `grep -n -E '\b(83|88|92|108)\b.*agents' README.md` shows one number for specialized agents, the same everywhere.
- [ ] The tools and workflows counts equal `ls .hanzo/agents/tools | wc -l` and `ls .hanzo/agents/workflows | wc -l`.
- [ ] The tree lists paths that exist (`.hanzo/agents/definitions`, `.hanzo/agents/workflows`, `.hanzo/agents/tools`).
- [ ] The counting rule appears once in the README and the pull request shows the commands used to recount.

Points: 75 (Hanzo Rewards, reputation points; not money; see https://hanzo.ai/bounty)

title: Fix 103 broken relative links in the README
body:
## Summary
103 relative links in `README.md` point to `agents/`, `workflows/` and `tools/` folders that do not exist at the repo root, so every agent link on GitHub is a 404. The files are under `.hanzo/agents/`.

## Evidence
Checked at `6ab6811`.

- `grep -o '](agents/[^)#]*)' README.md | wc -l` prints `101` (for example `README.md:335`, `agents/staff-engineer.md`; `:763`, `agents/README.md`). `grep -o '](workflows/[^)]*)' README.md | wc -l` and the same for `tools/` each print `1` (lines 764 and 765).
- `ls agents workflows tools` at the repo root: `No such file or directory` for all three.
- The targets exist one level down: every one of the 101 `agents/<name>.md` names exists as `.hanzo/agents/definitions/<name>.md` (a loop over the names finds none missing), and the other two are `.hanzo/agents/workflows/` and `.hanzo/agents/tools/`.
- `.github/CONTRIBUTING.md:7` links `.github/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md`, which resolves from that folder to `.github/.github/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md`; the file is `.github/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md`, so the link should be `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md`.

## What to do
Rewrite the prefixes in `README.md`: `](agents/` becomes `](.hanzo/agents/definitions/`, `](workflows/)` becomes `](.hanzo/agents/workflows/)`, `](tools/)` becomes `](.hanzo/agents/tools/)`. Fix the one link in `.github/CONTRIBUTING.md`. Do not touch counts or the structure tree; another issue covers those.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every relative link in `README.md` and `.github/CONTRIBUTING.md` resolves to an existing path (check with any markdown link checker, or a short script that tests each target with `test -e`).
- [ ] `git diff --stat` shows changes only in those two files, and the diff changes only link targets.
- [ ] Opening three of the links on the pull request's branch view lands on a file, not a 404.

title: Bug: vista deploy still breaks static hosts and platform adapters
body:
## Goal

Hunt and fix remaining **deployment** bugs in `vista deploy` and the hosted docs site.

`create-vista-app` no longer copies `Dockerfile` / `render.yaml` / `deploy/`. Platform files must come from the **engine** (`vista deploy`). That path is still buggy on some hosts.

## Known failure modes

Reproduce on `@vistagenic/vista@latest` (or `main` after #60 merges).

- [ ] **Cloudflare Pages (static)** — `/rsc/*` Flight fetches get rewritten to HTML instead of `.rsc` (double `_redirects` / identity `.rsc` rule). Client nav then full-reloads or hydrates from the wrong payload.
- [ ] **PPR shells** — loading HTML must not inline the finished page Flight (`ppr-page-content` leak).
- [ ] **Vercel / Netlify full SSR** — standalone `.vista/standalone/server.js` missing from the function pack; `--dry-run` should still emit a runnable handler.
- [ ] **Cloudflare Containers vs Pages** — `wrangler.toml` / Dockerfile emitted when the user wanted static Pages (or the reverse).
- [ ] **Render / Docker** — generated `startCommand` / `CMD` does not match `node .vista/standalone/server.js`.
- [ ] **Live regression** — https://vistajs.pages.dev view-source dumps extra `clientN-*.js` tags, or docs links do a full document reload.

## Steps

1. Scaffold: `npx create-vista-app@latest deploy-bounty-app --yes --skip-install` (no deploy files in the tree).
2. `npm install && npm run build`
3. `npx vista deploy --target <platform> --dry-run --force`
4. If claiming a live bug, also hit https://vistajs.pages.dev and https://vistajs.pages.dev/docs

## Pass

- Static Pages: HTML 200, `/rsc/docs` (no extra `.rsc` in the fetch URL) returns Flight, not HTML
- Standalone targets pack `server.js` + `node_modules` as documented
- `vista deploy` does not require hand-written `render.yaml` / `Dockerfile` in the app

## Fail notes

Paste target (`vercel` / `cloudflare` / `netlify` / `render` / `docker`), `--dry-run` log, status codes, and whether `deploy.output` was `static` or standalone.

## Related

Framework-wide bounty: file under the companion bounty issue.
Docs: https://vistajs.pages.dev/docs/deployment/vista-deploy-command

title: Bounty: hunt bugs across the entire Vista framework
body:
## Goal

Find real bugs anywhere in Vista — not only one feature. This is a framework-wide bounty hunt.

Scope is the published packages and the live docs app:

- `@vistagenic/vista` (RSC/SSR, `vista/link`, `vista/image`, `vista/theme`, `vista/auth`, `vista/ai`, `vista/stack`, `vista deploy`)
- `create-vista-app`
- Live site: https://vistajs.pages.dev
- Demo: `apps/vista-rag-demo`

## Surfaces to attack

- [ ] `npx create-vista-app@latest` → `dev` / `build` / `start`
- [ ] Client RSC navigation (no full reload) via `vista/link`
- [ ] Hydration, theme toggle, images
- [ ] `vista g api-init`, `vista g auth`, `vista g agent`
- [ ] AI streaming + tools; RAG retrieve + SSE
- [ ] `vista deploy` (Render, Vercel, Cloudflare, Netlify, Docker)
- [ ] Static CDN vs standalone Flight server
- [ ] Flashpack vs default engine

## How to claim

1. Open a **new issue** with a minimal repro (commands, Vista version, OS, logs).
2. Link this issue from that report.
3. Do **not** dump secrets. Redact API keys.
4. A patch PR is welcome **after** the bug is confirmed.

## Pass / bounty bar

A valid report has:

- Repro that fails on current `main` or `@vistagenic/vista@latest`
- Expected vs actual
- Whether it is generate-time, `vista dev`, production `start`, or deploy

Duplicates of #56–#59 (QA checklists) do not count unless you found a **new** failure.

## Related

- QA CLI: #56
- QA AI: #57
- QA RAG: #58
- QA fullstack / docs: #59

> **🐛 Bug** · 🟡 MEDIUM

> Cannot install a GitHub App at the organization level — it appears in My Apps but only an Edit button is available, no Install option.


## 🎯 Problem

The user owns a GitHub App and needs to install it for an organization. The app is visible under Developer settings → GitHub Apps → My Apps, but only the Edit button is exposed. There is no way to trigger an organization-level installation, which blocks the app from being granted access to org resources.

## 🔬 How to reproduce

1. Sign in to GitHub with the account that owns the GitHub App.
2. Navigate to Settings → Developer settings → GitHub Apps.
3. Open the My Apps tab and select the target app.
4. Look at the action area on the right side of the app details page.
5. Attempt to install the app on an organization (either via the page or via the org's Install integration flow).

## 🎯 Expected vs Actual

**Expected:** An Install option (or an Install dropdown listing available organizations) is shown, allowing an org owner to install the app on the chosen organization.
**Actual:** Only the Edit button is shown. No Install / Install on organization option is available, so org-level installation cannot be initiated.

## 📋 Scope

- GitHub Apps developer settings UI (My Apps detail page)
- GitHub App installation flow / API
- GitHub App manifest and ownership configuration
- Organization permissions for the requesting user

_Files/components in-scope for this fix. Anything else → new bounty._

## 🚧 Constraints

- User is acting at the organization level, not on a personal account.
- App already exists and is owned by the user (it shows in My Apps), so creation is not the blocker.
- User may or may not have org owner rights — this needs to be verified during investigation.

_Hard requirements. The fix MUST respect these (e.g. "must work at org level, not just user account")._

- **Repo**: [Zimb/zimb](https://github.com/Zimb/zimb)

- [ ] The app's detail page exposes an Install action (button or dropdown).

title: Etapa 5: flujo de propuesta y moderacion de mapas de usuario
body:
Parte de #2 (modo construcción). Depende del espacio de mapas de usuario.

## El problema

Contenido subido por cualquiera necesita revisión antes de ser parte del mundo. Sin esto, el primer mapa con contenido ofensivo o con gráficos plagiados es un problema para el proyecto, no para quien lo subió.

Publicación directa no es una opción.

## Alcance

1. **Flujo de estados**: borrador → propuesto → en revisión → publicado o rechazado.
2. **Cola de moderación** para revisores, con vista previa del mapa sin tener que entrar a jugarlo.
3. **Rechazo con motivo**, que le llegue al autor para que pueda corregir y volver a proponer.
4. **Reportes**: cualquier jugador puede reportar un mapa ya publicado, y eso lo devuelve a la cola.
5. **Despublicar** un mapa que ya estaba vivo, si aparece un problema después.

## Qué tiene que poder revisar el moderador

- Los gráficos subidos por el autor, que es donde va a estar la mayoría de los problemas
- El nombre del mapa y cualquier texto que haya puesto (carteles, nombres de NPCs)
- Si el mapa tiene zonas inalcanzables o trampas de las que no se puede salir
- Si respeta las cuotas

## Automatizable

Buena parte de la revisión se puede pre-filtrar:

- Detección de tiles bloqueados que dejan regiones aisladas
- Chequeo de que existe al menos un camino desde el punto de entrada
- Límites de cantidad ya validados antes de llegar a la cola
- Lista de palabras prohibidas en nombres y textos

Cuanto más se automatice, menos trabajo humano por mapa, que es lo que decide si esto escala.

## Criterios de aceptación

- [ ] Un mapa propuesto no es visible para otros jugadores hasta ser aprobado
- [ ] El revisor puede ver el mapa y sus assets sin jugarlo
- [ ] Rechazar exige un motivo, y el autor lo recibe
- [ ] Un mapa publicado puede ser reportado y vuelve a la cola
- [ ] Los chequeos automáticos corren antes de que el mapa llegue a un humano
- [ ] Tests del flujo completo de estados

## Nota

Conviene definir desde el principio quién modera y cómo se suman moderadores. Si depende de una sola persona, la cola se convierte en el cuello de botella y el sistema muere por ahí.
